newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW-ING Manila unit to go into insurance.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ING Manila unit to go into insurance.

text.p: ING Bank's Philippine unit plans to enter the life insurance business, a bank official said on Friday.

"We are going into the life insurance business. Right now 90 percent of the (life insurance) business here is controlled by four or five companies," Philippine country manager Renato de Guzman said in an interview.
ING Bank is one of 10 foreign banks that have been allowed to set up since last year with the liberalisation of the banking sector.

"We think with an improvement in consumer incomes, there would be tremendous opportunities for insurance," De Guzman said, citing the country's increasing gross national product growth which was expected to rise to seven percent in 1996 from 5.7 percent last year.
"But it's not going to be easy getting into the sector because some firms have dominated it for over 50 years," he added.
De Guzman said ING's new life insurance business would depend on a combination of direct sales through its branches as well as an agency network to distribute its products.
ING Bank's direct insurance distribution would however be limited as it has just six branches in the country.
But ING Bank hopes to turn its insurance agency force into a distribution window for its banking products as well.
"We are thinking of not just an insurance agent but a financial advisor who sells all products," de Guzman said.

Banking industry analysts said if the distribution network succeeded, it would mean the bank would also widen the reach of its main business interests which are in consumer savings and private banking as well as asset management.

Under the rules, foreign banks are limited in the number of branches they can set up. Of the permitted six, a foreign bank may set up three in any place they want while the other half have to be areas specified by the government.
The government issued the rule to ensure a wider geographical distribution of foreign banks in the country.
With the takeover of Barings last year, ING Bank acquired a presence in the local stock market.
ING Barings is one of the big foreign brokers in Manila and has had a large share of the market for initial public offerings of shares, de Guzman said.
